title: OSI vs. TCP/IP Models
description: Interactive SVG comparison of the 7-layer OSI model and the 4-layer TCP/IP model, with dashed layer-mapping lines, per-layer hover tooltips (protocols and example controls), and a 'where attacks live' annotation column.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity
chapter_title: Network Security Foundations: Protocols, Firewalls, and Detection

educational.topic: The OSI and TCP/IP network models and the layers where attacks occur
learningObjectives: Map each of the seven OSI layers to its corresponding TCP/IP layer.
Identify example protocols at each layer of both models.
Associate common attacks (ARP spoofing, IP spoofing, SYN floods, SQL injection) with the layer they target.
educational.prerequisites: Basic familiarity with IP, TCP, and the idea of network protocols.

pedagogical.modelType: static two-column comparison with hover reveals
controls: Hover/tap any OSI layer for protocols and an example control
Hover/tap any TCP/IP layer for the OSI layers it spans and a control
Read the dashed lines mapping OSI layers to TCP/IP layers
Read the 'where attacks live' callouts (L2, L3, L4, L7)
pedagogical.assessment: Students place a given protocol or attack at the correct layer in both models and explain why TCP/IP collapses OSI 5-7 into one application layer.
misconceptionsAddressed: Believing OSI and TCP/IP layers map one-to-one.
Assuming TLS lives at exactly one fixed OSI layer.
